title: Transformation Magic
text: Some time later, on a certain afternoon during a day off, I say.
“Um, let’s see…”

Since the academy was also off that day, Itsuki had returned to the village via portal and was doing something in his room, book in hand. Father, Ren, and I happened to all be together when we came across him like this.
“What are you up to, Itsuki?”
“Ah, I’m just reviewing some magic that’ll come up in class. Apparently it’s fine if I just observe, but since I’ve got the chance, I figured I’d try to learn it myself.”
“Being a teacher sounds rough,” Ren said, peering into the crystal ball Itsuki was fiddling with.
“Heh… so it’s like learning alongside the students.”
“So, what kind of magic is it?”
“Yes, what I’m reviewing this time is Polymorph. It’s called Transformation Magic.”
“There’s magic like that? Is it maybe the kind Filo and everyone, and Gaelion-chan, and Sadeena-san use?”
“No, apparently that’s a different kind of magic entirely. This one’s strictly for humans to temporarily change their appearance.”
Hmm… now that I think of it, I recall Father mentioning something like this from a magic shop in Melromarc.
“Would that spinning wheel for making transformation clothes at the Melromarc magic shop be for this spell, I wonder?”
“Could be. Unfortunately, if someone transformed uses magic, it’s apparently obvious right away who they really are, but in the past it was reportedly used for things like infiltration.”
Even now, the Shadows apparently still use this magic sometimes, Itsuki added.
“Sounds pretty interesting. I kind of want to try it too,” Father said.
“Hmm… can you transform into any animal you want?”
“Cat and dog monsters seem to be the most common. Apparently some people can even become mice.”
“Whoa… that’s got a real witch vibe, very dreamy. It’d be fun to use it to surprise everyone in the village.”
…Oh? I’m vaguely recalling something now.
“Now that I think of it, in the peaceful world, I believe Father tried using that spell once and… changed his appearance, if I recall correctly.”
He’d immediately turned back after being amazed such magic existed.
“Even Heroes can use this magic? I guess the Legendary Weapons don’t reject it or anything?”
“Probably because it’s activated by one’s own will? Though in our case, our true identities would probably be figured out immediately.”
“True, but still. It’s got that otherworldly feel to it, you know? Not just offensive spells and healing spells all the time—let’s give it a try.”
“Sure. Sounds fun,” Ren said, clearly game. Well, if he’s in, I’ll follow Father’s lead too, I say.
“So how do we do this?”

“First you draw a magic circle in a small room, and there was a catalyst in the village storehouse, so we set that in the center of the room. Then whoever wants to transform just needs to stand in the circle and cast the spell.”
Oh? So there was a catalyst like that lying around. Had someone bought it and stashed it in the storehouse?
“I see, something like this then.”
“Yes, and now for the spell. I’ll cast it on everyone too. The characters floating up are…”
And so, as we all gathered around and looked at the catalyst while chanting the spell, our respective weapons, the catalyst, and the magic circle in the room all lit up.
“Ooh! This seems amazing.”
“Hmm…”
“Indeed.”
I’m surprised the weapons are reacting at all. It’s not like they’re resisting—it feels more like they’re sensing the flow of magic power.
“Ah, feels like it’s going to take hold nicely.”
“Guess it’s because there’s no hostile intent in the spell?”
“Apparently the dragon transformation magic Gaelion-chan talks about gets rejected by the Legendary Weapons. Since this is just temporary, I think it should be fine?”
Both Father and Ren seemed thoroughly intrigued by this so-called Transformation Magic. I was looking forward to it myself, I say.
“Source of power, Bow Hero commands thee. Unravel the workings of all creation once more, and alter the forms of these persons.”
“Al Four Fairy Morph!? Wait, that’s wr—!”
And then—poof! Smoke billowed up in an instant. My vision was engulfed in smoke, and I couldn’t see a thing. What’s more, some cloth came draping down from somewhere above.
“Cough, cough… Itsuki, that’s way too much smoke.”
“It’s smoky. Also, wasn’t the spell name wrong just now?”
“Yes, it was supposed to activate a spell called Al Polymorph.”
“It was named Al Four Fairy Morph, I believe.”
“Guess that means it failed, huh?”

While we were having this conversation, the smoke quickly dissipated. I moved the cloth aside and checked my surroundings. And there before me… Father’s clothes had fallen off, empty. The same was true for Itsuki and Ren. Wriggling out from the collar of Father’s discarded clothes… came a penguin wearing a Santa hat and holding a shield.
“Uh, um…”

As the penguin turned its face toward where Itsuki’s clothes lay collapsed in a heap, a squirrel likewise poked its face out from within them. And from where Ren’s clothes lay crumpled on the floor… for some reason, Keel poked her head out. Then the penguin turned its face toward me. This penguin… looks familiar. It’s the spitting image of the Peckle, the natives spoken of on Cal Mira Island and elsewhere. It’s identical to the mascot costumes Father tends to acquire with alarming frequency.
“Um, so I guess the Polymorph took hold properly? Riska.”
“Who’s Riska? Oh, right, it said something about needing to prepare clothes beforehand—I completely forgot about that.”
Wriggling free, the penguin—judging by the voice and the shield it’s holding, that’s Father—climbed out of the pile of discarded clothes and began folding them up.
“I see… so I suppose we can call this a success, result-wise. Riska.”
This Keel-looking thing is saying something. Everyone was emerging from their fallen clothes to check themselves over.
“So I said, who’s Riska? If we’re going by that logic, you’re a Peckle, and that one over there is an Inulto, aren’t you?”
“Um, so the one holding a gun—that’d be Itsuki, right?”
“Yes, that’s correct.”
When Father asked the squirrel, the squirrel—Itsuki—nodded in confirmation.
“You must be Keel, I take it.”
“Nope. Judge by the weapon. So the rabbit-hedgehog thing is Motoyasu, huh?”

I addressed the one I thought was Keel, only to be told I was wrong. It certainly looks exactly like Keel to me, but judging by the voice and such, that’s probably Ren. I checked my own appearance in a mirror in the room. And there, standing with a spear in hand, wearing a Santa hat, was a rabbit. There was no mistaking it—that was a Usauni!
When I touched my face, I felt a fluffy, soft texture. My height had shrunk considerably.
“How should I put this… we’ve all become quite fancy-looking, haven’t we,” Itsuki said.
“Seems like it. Ren looks like he became a dog… so maybe not that different in essence?”
“Who knows. Motoyasu’s a rabbit… suits him perfectly.”
“Ah… yes, Motoyasu-kun really does suit being a rabbit.”
I’d been praised by what appeared to be Father-the-penguin!
“Behold, Usauni Motoyasu has arrived, I say!”
Hop! Just like that! When I struck a pose, Father applauded me. Pat pat, indeed.
“So, why exactly have we all transformed into the appearances of the natives passed down in legend at various training grounds around the world?”
“Beats me… I’m not entirely sure myself either. I’ve observed and listened in on the students’ classes, and nothing like this happened during my first experiment.”
“I tried this out of curiosity, but this shortness is really inconvenient. How do we undo this spell?”
“Apparently the remaining transformation time is supposed to display in your field of vision, but…”
“There’s nothing here, Itsuki. Just how strongly did you cast this thing?”
“I didn’t construct it to be that complicated! Just wait a moment. Um, let’s see…”
Itsuki spread open the dropped spellbook and began flipping through the pages.

“It should undo itself automatically over time, or you can chant a release spell to dispel it immediately. I’ve gotten fairly good at reading the characters, but it still takes me a bit of time to read through.”
“Let me borrow that for a moment, I say.”
Thanks to my time loops, I have a deeper understanding of these characters than most. I checked over the spellbook Itsuki had been reading.
Beginning of the Fluffy Chapter.
